questions.def: We use 'until' to indicate the duration leading up to a specific point in time.
questions.question: ___ the bell rings, students are expected to remain seated.

questions.def: 'By the time' indicates an action completed before another action in the future.
questions.question: She will have finished the report ___ you arrive.

questions.def: 'After' can be followed by a gerund when the subject is clear.
questions.question: They will leave ___ dinner.

questions.def: 'Upon' expresses immediacy after an action.
questions.question: ___ having submitted the application, he felt relieved.

questions.def: 'Once' introduces a condition that triggers a subsequent action.
questions.question: ___ the evidence is presented, the judge will make a ruling.

questions.def: Past perfect participle indicates completed action before the main verb.
questions.question: ___ for the signal, they prepared to launch.

questions.def: 'During' refers to the period when something happens.
questions.question: ___ the storm, the power went out.

questions.def: 'As soon as' denotes immediate succession.
questions.question: I will contact you ___ I have more information.

questions.def: Past perfect participle shows action completed before another.
questions.question: ___, they began the presentation.

questions.def: 'Prior to' means before a specific time.
questions.question: ___ the meeting, please submit your reports.

questions.def: 'Once' indicates a specific starting point.
questions.question: ___ the new law takes effect, we must comply.

questions.def: Past perfect participle: action finished before another.
questions.question: ___ the task, they celebrated.

questions.def: 'During' refers to a period when something happens.
questions.question: ___ the conference, I hope to network.

questions.def: 'As' indicates a parallel increase or simultaneous action.
questions.question: ___ the deadline approaches, anxiety increases.

questions.def: Past perfect participle indicates completed action.
questions.question: ___ the report, he submitted it.

questions.def: 'Following' indicates immediately after something.
questions.question: ___ the presentation, questions were welcomed.

questions.def: 'Once' indicates a completed action and its consequence.
questions.question: ___ I had finished, I went home.

questions.def: Past perfect participle shows action completed before another.
questions.question: ___, he aced the test.

questions.def: 'Subsequent to' means after a specific event.
questions.question: ___ the lecture, a Q&A session will follow.

questions.def: 'Once' sets a condition for a subsequent action.
questions.question: ___ the project is completed, we celebrate.

questions.def: Past perfect participle denotes an action finished first.
questions.question: ___ dinner, he went out.

questions.def: 'Following' indicates immediate succession.
questions.question: ___ her presentation, everyone applauded.

questions.def: 'Once' introduces a condition that must be met.
questions.question: ___ you finish your work, you can leave.

questions.def: Use 'has been collected' after 'once' to show a completed action.
questions.question: Once the data ___, we can begin the analysis.

questions.def: 'Once' introduces a time clause indicating when the report will be written.
questions.question: ___ the experiment is concluded, a report will be written.

questions.def: Use the present simple 'submit' in time clauses referring to the future.
questions.question: By the time you ___ the application, the deadline will have passed.

questions.def: 'Scarcely/hardly...when' requires infinitive after 'begun'.
questions.question: Scarcely had they begun ___, when the power went out.

questions.def: 'As soon as' indicates immediacy after receiving further information.
questions.question: I will contact you ___ I receive further information.

questions.def: 'Having finished' introduces a perfect participle clause indicating completed action.
questions.question: ___ the report, please send it to the editor.

questions.def: Use present simple 'makes' after 'before' to refer to future.
questions.question: Before the committee ___ a decision, all evidence must be presented.
